evidence: deepseek checks `if p1 + p2 > T` and running totals; gpt-oss records `p1 + p2 > T` then uses `sum1 > T` or `LOAD 2`; qwen comments `Check for single job too long` and `Check for machine overload`; glm performs the same three tests
affordance_in_statement: Exactly one of the following reasons always applies, and you should print the one that holds: "A single job is too long" if some job's two processing times add up to more than T; "A machine is overloaded" if the total work on machine 1 or machine 2 exceeds T.
removal_suggestion: Remove the explicit exhaustive dichotomy and its direct if-and-only-if tests. Present the certificate requirement through a quantified schedule-level argument, with the JOB and LOAD outputs still defined but requiring the solver to derive why the selected certificate is valid rather than handing out the scan conditions.
